fields.title: The Log as a Product
fields.keyTakeaway: The log transitions from a cost center to a feature when it becomes available to the client and starts signaling anomalies.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: The log exists, no one uses it. Why is it there then?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: A log that exists only for compliance is an expense without return. With minor refinement, it becomes a feature people pay for.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: **Exists.** Data is written, available upon request through support. Minimum for a questionnaire.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **Available.** The client views and filters themselves in the interface. Relieves load from support and increases trust.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **Operational.** The log not only shows the past but signals: unusual activity, mass export, login from a new location, a series of access denials.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: The third level turns the log into a security feature. What is worth signaling:
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: *Mass export.* An employee exported ten times the usual amount. *Access off-schedule.* At night, from another country. *Series of denials.* A sign of permission brute-forcing. *Actions after dismissal.* Requires connection with the HR system, but partially visible through inactivity.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: Who to signal — a product decision: the client administrator, us, both.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: Separate value — **dispute resolution.** "Who changed the price" and "who canceled the order" are questions arising constantly. The log answers in seconds.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: The log went through all three levels in a year.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: First version — recording only, access via support. Over a quarter 40 requests of the type "who did this", each taking half an hour of work.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Second — interface in the account. Requests dropped to 4 per quarter.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Third — signals. Three configured: export of more than 500 records at a time, login from a new country, more than 10 access denials per hour. Sent to the partner administrator.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: The first month of signals produced two real cases: in one chain a former employee was logging in via unrevoked access, in another an integrator was exporting the full order database daily instead of incremental synchronization — not malicious, but load and extra data for a third party.
fields.sections/3/blocks/5/text: In enterprise negotiations, a log with signals closes three questionnaire items at once and is mentioned as an advantage.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Signals get noisy and stop being read if thresholds are chosen poorly. Start with two or three with clearly anomalous thresholds.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: The log transitions from a cost center to a feature when it becomes available to the client and starts signaling anomalies.
